subject: Dedicated capacity discovery snapshot & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@skylark.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery snapshot & next steps

Hi James / Maya —

Thanks again for the 30-min sync earlier. Quick recap so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. I attached the meeting notes and a preliminary capacity worksheet.

Key pain points we heard
- Unpredictable token cost and tail latency on current multi-tenant endpoints (spikes during batch processing windows).
- Regulatory requirement for tenant isolation for certain financial workloads (data cannot be co-mingled).
- Need for predictable throughput during market open (target sustained TPS ~250, short bursts to ~400).

Current stack overview (from our notes)
- Inference: on-prem K8s + inference containers (mixed FP16/INT8) with a Redis-based KV cache.
- Models: mix of open LLMs and a proprietary re-ranker.
- Orchestration: homegrown autoscaler primarily CPU/GPU node scaling.

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit
- 99th percentile generation latency < 200ms at peak TPS for short sequences (<=128 tokens).
- Dedicated GPU pool with per-tenant isolation and KMS integration for keys.
- Autoscale/burst behavior that can accommodate market-open spikes to ~400 TPS without impact to other tenants.
- Clear price delta vs hosted with predictable unit economics for committed capacity.

Assumptions we used in the worksheet
- 60% of traffic is sub-128 tokens; batchability expected during non-interactive jobs.
- Peak window 09:30–09:45 ET daily for ~45 minutes.

Immediate next steps
1) Marcus to run a short technical checklist and request a 24-hour sample workload (or a synthetic trace) to refine the capacity calc (Marcus: will send specifics).
2) Schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive next week to go over perf targets and networking/KMS needs — proposed dates in the Calendly link below.
3) Ops: procurement touchpoint to surface contract timeline and any security docs (James / Maya, loop in procurement@skylark.ai when ready).

Attachments: Mtg-Notes-20260415.pdf (notes), Prelim-Capacity-Calc.xlsx (worksheet), Redwood-Dedicated-one-pager.pdf

If this aligns, I’ll block the deep-dive and Marcus will send the workload template.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery snapshot & next steps

Thanks Olga — this is helpful and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side:

- That 250 TPS target is for our primary scoring endpoint (short model path). The re-ranker has a lower TPS but higher memory per request.
- We can share a 48-hour trace from last month; it contains the market-open spikes and some synthetic batch jobs we run overnight. Is S3 a safe place for you to pull it, or do you want a temporary signed URL?
- On isolation: we need to ensure that audit logs are retained for 12 months and that keys are customer-managed.

For next steps — happy to do the tech deep-dive on April 22 at 11am ET if that works for Marcus and you. Procurement: once we get a ballpark commit estimate we can loop in legal.

James
VP Product, Skylark AI
james.park@skylark.ai | +1 212-555-0199

[Inline: link to sample trace (will send via shared link)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@skylark.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@skylark.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery snapshot & next steps

James / Maya —

Great, appreciate the trace offer. S3 signed URL is perfect. To make the capacity calc and an initial perf target we need the following from your trace:
- A 24–48 hour compressed trace (JSON or msgpack) with timestamped request sizes and response token counts.
- A brief manifest of which requests hit the re-ranker vs the generator.
- Any sequence-length distribution for the scoring endpoint (percentiles).

What I’ll do before the deep-dive
- Run the sketch capacity model against your trace and produce a heatmap of expected GPU utilization and a candidate pool sizing with burst headroom.
- Prepare a short list of networking/KMS questions (VPC peering, egress rules, customer KMS ARN patterns).

If you can send the link by EOD Monday (Apr 20) I’ll have an initial sizing and perf targets to present on Apr 22.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick alignment.

Summary of agreed operational plan
- James: share the 48-hour trace via a signed S3 URL by EOD today. Include the re-ranker manifest if possible.
- Marcus: will run the preliminary sizing and share a heatmap + recommended pool config by Apr 22 (for the deep-dive).
- Olga/Vivek: we’ll prepare a two-option commercial sketch — 6-month pilot commit and 12-month reserved pool — and surface the differential so procurement can prioritize.

Tentative deep-dive: Apr 22, 11:00am–12:00pm ET (Calendly link sent). I’ve also attached the one-pager for your internal folks to review ahead of the call.

If procurement has any required contract language around data residency or indemnity, please flag ahead of the deep-dive so legal can be prepared.

Look forward to the next call.

Best,
